edges.effect_quant: In a placebo-controlled 6-week study of 22 overweight or obese adults, 30 g/day oligofructose reduced hunger area under the curve and motivation to eat while tending to raise PYY; in a randomized crossover study of 21 overweight or obese adults, inulin-propionate ester incorporated into food products significantly reduced ad libitum energy intake; however, a small 7-participant crossover pilot using a 10 g pre-meal inulin preload found no acute reduction in energy intake or appetite.
edges.population: overweight or obese adults given inulin-type fructans, oligofructose, or inulin-derived propionate-delivery supplements in short human intervention trials
edges.mechanism: Inulin-type fructans are fermented by colonic microbes into short-chain fatty acids that can stimulate satiety hormones such as PYY and GLP-1, slow appetite return, and modestly reduce subsequent energy intake.
edges.summary: Inulin-type supplementation can enhance satiety in some human studies, especially when fermentation products reach the colon effectively and when subjective hunger rather than body weight is the endpoint. The benefit is real but modest, and not every acute preload study detects it.
edges.caveats: Effects differ by chain length, formulation, dose, age, and whether the intervention uses plain inulin versus inulin-propionate ester. Some studies show lower hunger ratings without clear reductions in total daily energy intake or body weight.
